title: Fed hawkishness and oil supply shocks drive USD, gold and INR pressure
changed: The Fed minutes confirmed a hawkish bias and a continuation of balance‑sheet runoff, keeping the dollar on the rise. A stronger dollar pushed gold to a one‑year low and added pressure on the rupee, while the RBI’s repo rate stayed near 5.6%, anchoring short‑term G‑sec yields.

Hurricane Isaias caused repeated shut‑ins of Gulf Coast crude production, holding Brent crude above $90 a barrel. The elevated Brent price lifted India’s oil import bill, fed INR depreciation risk and buoyed energy‑related equities.

FII inflows lifted the Nifty 50 to multi‑month highs, but profit‑booking and a broader AI‑related equity rotation pulled the index down from the 25,000 technical level. SEBI’s proposal to drop extra FPI disclosure requirements could lower compliance costs and revive foreign inflows.

RBI’s liquidity operations showed tight short‑term funding: a 1.9‑times oversubscribed 3‑day VRR auction and low participation in the reverse repo auction kept short‑end yields around 6.6%. The central bank also switched ₹21,000 cr of short‑dated debt into longer maturities, smoothing the sovereign supply curve.

Regulatory signals surfaced on the tax front: the budget is expected to address LTCG and STT rates, while FEMA compounding powers were delegated to RBI regional offices, shortening compliance resolution for cross‑border transactions. Both could affect net returns on equity portfolios and corporate FX exposure.

threads.name: US dollar strength
threads.note: Fed minutes keep the dollar firm, pulling gold lower and adding depreciation pressure on the rupee; short‑term yields stay elevated.

threads.name: Brent crude supply constraint
threads.note: Hurricane Isaias keeps Brent above $90, raising India’s import bill and supporting energy‑sector equities while weighing on the INR.

threads.name: Indian equity flows and AI rotation
threads.note: FII buying lifted the Nifty, but profit‑taking and a global pullback from AI‑heavy stocks triggered a sell‑off; SEBI’s pending FPI‑disclosure easing could offset outflows.

threads.name: RBI liquidity management
threads.note: Oversubscribed VRR auction and a long‑dated bond switch reduce near‑term funding stress, anchoring short‑end yields and supporting sovereign financing.
